findings.evidence: "The people operations office publishes the reimbursement log each quarter" vs. "The benefits team publishes the reimbursement log after every open enrollment period"
findings.fix: Determine the correct publication schedule and responsible team, then replace both statements with a single accurate statement.
findings.location: Program Overview, first paragraph and Questions and Updates section
findings.violation: The document provides two conflicting statements about when the reimbursement log is published (quarterly vs. after open enrollment) and which team publishes it (people operations office vs. benefits team).

findings.evidence: "the IT asset group tracks the stipend budget each quarter. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Clarify whether these are the same team or different teams, and explain what information each team maintains.
findings.violation: Unclear who maintains the stipend budget information - the IT asset group tracks it, but staff request it from the benefits team, leaving their relationship undefined.

findings.evidence: "However, reimbursement is not available without a completed receipt."
findings.fix: Replace "However" with "Additionally" or restructure to clarify that receipt submission is a separate eligibility requirement.
findings.violation: The transition word "However" does not logically connect to the eligibility conditions listed in the previous paragraph; receipt requirements are different from the conditions already stated.

findings.evidence: "Then, the review takes longer because the manager who normally handles it is traveling; the backup reviewer who covers for absences was not told that the request needs sign-off before the portal releases the confirmation email."
findings.fix: Either remove this sentence or rewrite it as a general policy statement, such as "The review may take longer if the primary manager is unavailable; backup reviewers must be notified of pending requests."
findings.location: How to Apply section, third paragraph
findings.violation: This sentence describes a current operational problem rather than a policy, and it is unclear whether it is meant to explain a permanent policy condition or document a temporary issue.

findings.evidence: "The manager approves items pursuant to internal discretion, notwithstanding the standard review checklist."
findings.fix: Rewrite as: "The manager approves items using the standard review checklist and may exercise judgment for items not covered by the checklist."
findings.violation: The phrasing is unnecessarily formal and contradictory - it states that managers use discretion "notwithstanding" (despite) a standard checklist, which is unclear and suggests the checklist can be ignored.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite as: "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition. The company may request photo verification of equipment once per year."
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, first sentence
findings.violation: The sentence mixes pronouns inconsistently (you/we) and uses vague language ("may ask") without specifying how, when, or why photo checks will be requested.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee."
findings.fix: Replace "Similarly" with "Additionally" or begin a new paragraph.
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, second sentence
findings.violation: The transition word "Similarly" does not logically connect to the previous sentence about photo checks; the sentences address unrelated topics.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review."
findings.fix: Either delete this section as redundant with "Program Coordination," or retitle it "Payment Process" and define what a "stipend item" is in the opening sentence.
findings.violation: The section is titled "Terminology Notes" but explains processes rather than defining terms. The term "stipend item" is used repeatedly throughout but is never defined.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Provide the complete ordered list of all steps required to submit a request, such as "1. Confirm eligibility. 2. Upload receipt. 3. Select equipment category. 4. Submit for review."
findings.violation: The section header indicates multiple request steps, but the content only describes what the process "begins with," leaving the full procedure incomplete.

findings.evidence: "The benefits team publishes the reimbursement log after every open enrollment period. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Delete this duplicate "Overview" section and consolidate all program information into the "Program Overview" section at the beginning.
findings.violation: This section duplicates the "Program Overview" section at the beginning of the document, creating confusion about which statement is accurate and cluttering the document.

findings.evidence: "Also, the deposit happens in order to offset costs the employee already paid at this point in time."
findings.fix: Rewrite as: "This reimbursement compensates employees for equipment costs they have already incurred."
findings.violation: The phrasing is unnecessarily wordy and uses imprecise language ("at this point in time") that obscures the simple meaning.
